title: What is Semantic Segmentation
text: Semantic Segmentation means labeling every pixel of an object in an image. Annotators draw over the image to mark each object, so the model can recognize and locate it.
notes:

Rear mode : if there is an existing shape, draw behind that existing shape

title: Project overview
text: The purpose of this project is to create a dataset for AI to recognize people and use the AI to create a photobooth-type media art experience that can be combined with various IPS.
Face, Body, Age, Gender, Image brightness

title: Project overview
text: All people in the image are labeling targets

title: Labeling Criteria
text: 1. Bounding Box: Face= The person’s head, face, and neck must be contained within the bounding box area.
Hair, hats, headbands, bag, etc are not include in the bounding box area.
Please note that neck, face until forehead is labeling area to b-box.

title: Labeling Criteria
text: 2. Attributes: Gender, Age, and Image brightness= Please select the correct age, gender, and image brightness seen in the image.

title: Labeling Criteria
text: 3. Polygon: Body= The person’s whole-body outline must be labeled with the polygon tool.
Hair, bags, hat, headbands, etc are labeling target for the body class.

title: Introduction to three-dimensional space and the Principles of LiDAR
text: Introduction to three-dimensional space and the Principles of LiDAR

title: Introduction to three-dimensional space
text: 3D (3-dimensional): We normally talk about dimensions as measurements in a direction. Real-world objects exist in 3D space, allowing for deeper perception by using height, width, and depth.

title: Basics of spatial coordinates and dimensions
text: Basics of spatial coordinates and dimensions
Spatial coordinates use X, Y, and Z axes to locate points in 3D space.
The x-coordinate represents the horizontal position (left or right).
The y-coordinate represents the vertical position (up or down).
The z-coordinate represents the depth or position along the third dimension.

title: Uses of spatial coordinates and dimensions
text: Uses of spatial coordinates and dimensions
Dimensions add depth to objects, enhancing realism.

Technology and Computing: In the realm of technology and computing, spatial coordinates are vital for computer graphics, virtual reality, and simulation. They enable the creation of realistic 3D environments, immersive experiences, and accurate simulations. Examples of spatial coordinates in technology and computing include robotics and automation, virtual reality and augmented reality, and GPS navigation

title: Uses of spatial coordinates and dimensions
text: Uses of spatial coordinates and dimensions
Navigation and Mapping: Spatial coordinates enable accurate navigation and mapping, allowing people to find locations, plan routes, and understand geographic relationships.

Aid in the development of Autonomous Vehicles (AVs): Spatial coordinates are pivotal for autonomous vehicles (AVs), guiding mapping, navigation, and object detection. They facilitate localization, map creation, and path planning. AVs share spatial data for safe intersection management.

title: LiDAR Fundamentals
text: LiDAR, or Light Detection and Ranging, is a remote sensing technology that uses laser pulses to measure distances to objects or surfaces. It creates detailed 3D maps for various applications, such as mapping, navigation, and urban planning.

title: Uses of LiDAR Technology
text: Autonomous Vehicles (AVs): LiDAR helps AVs "see" and navigate by detecting objects and creating maps.
Aerial Surveying: LiDAR -equipped aircraft and drones accurately map terrain, forests, and cities.
Geographic Information Systems (GIS): LiDAR data helps create detailed maps for urban planning and environmental management.

title: Uses of LiDAR Technology
text: Archeology: LiDAR uncovers hidden archaeological sites by scanning terrain with precision.
Forestry Monitoring: LiDAR measures tree heights and monitors forest health.
Disaster Management: LiDAR maps disaster areas to aid rescue operations and assess damage.

text: 3D Point Clouds:   - Captures reflections to form point clouds.   - Represents specific locations in 3D.Precision and Accuracy:   - Provides high-precision measurements.   - Ensures detailed and accurate 3D models.

text: Introduction to the PCD Project, Guide, and the Process of Labeling.

title: Introduction to PCD Project
text: PCD is termed Point Cloud Data. These are points that represent data picked up by a LiDAR signal.

title: Why does this PCD Project exist?
text: Why does this PCD Project exist?
Accurate Object Detection and Recognition: Autonomous vehicles need to detect and recognize various objects in their environment, such as pedestrians, vehicles, cyclists, and obstacles.

Depth Perception and Spatial Awareness: This allows autonomous vehicles to perceive the distance to objects, which is crucial for making safe driving decisions such as braking, lane changes, and avoiding collisions.

title: Why does this PCD Project exist?
text: Why does this PCD Project exist?
Environment Understanding: 3D PCD labelling helps in understanding the layout of the environment, including road boundaries, lane markings, traffic signs, and other infrastructure elements.
Enhanced Safety and Reliability: Accurate 3D PCD labelling improves the safety and reliability of autonomous vehicles by reducing the risk of misinterpreting the surroundings.
